title: Risk factors for post-intensive care syndrome in adult intensive care patients: a retrospective analysis of routine clinical data
summary: After treatment in an intensive care unit, some people have long-lasting problems such as muscle weakness, difficulties with concentration and memory, or anxiety. This is called post-intensive care syndrome (PICS). This study uses patient records to examine how often factors that make PICS more likely are documented in patients of a cardiological intensive care and intermediate care unit. Only existing treatment data are analysed. Patients are not examined or interviewed additionally.

interventions.name:
Adult cases of the cardiological ICU and IMC, discharged or transferred in 2025 (random sample).
Retrospective observation, no intervention. Previously documented routine data are analysed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Discharge or transfer from the ICU and IMC between 01 January 2025 and 31 December 2025; combined length of stay in the ICU and IMC of at least 24 hours. If a person had several stays in the period, only the first is included. A random sample of 10 % is drawn from all cases meeting these criteria.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who died in the ICU or IMC; exclusively palliative treatment goal decided at admission; readmissions within the period; cases in which the documentation of the stay is unavailable or incomplete.
